# Best overall: BLUETTI AC200L

<badge color="success">My top recommendation</badge> <badge color="secondary">$899 listed price</badge>

Based on the 17 pages you supplied, I'd choose the **<Entity value="BLUETTI AC200L" category="product" />** for an RV. It offers the best combination of RV-specific connectivity, power output, battery capacity, solar charging and price under your $900 budget.

<AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view" aspectRatio="16:9" width="100%" fit="contain"/>

## How the top contenders compare

| Feature | BLUETTI AC200L | Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | Renogy PowerStation 2000 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Price | **$899** | $899.99 | $849 |
| Capacity | 2,048 Wh | ~2,000 Wh | 2,048 Wh |
| Continuous output | 2,400 W | — | 2,400 W |
| Battery | LiFePO4 | LiFePO4 | LiFePO4 |
| Weight | — | 41.7 lb | — |
| RV TT-30 outlet | **Yes** | Not established | Not established |
| Solar input | **1,200 W** | — | — |
| Warranty | 5 years | — | — |

Sources: [Dealectric comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv), [BuyerSheet comparison](https://buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/2kwh/), [Renogy official product page](https://www.renogy.com/collections/all/products/power-station-2000).

## Why I'd buy the AC200L

1. **RV-ready TT-30 outlet:** This is its biggest advantage. You can connect a standard 30-amp RV shore-power cord directly, without needing an adapter.
2. **Strong output:** 2,400 W continuous is enough for many RV appliances, including a refrigerator, microwave or coffee maker, subject to their individual power requirements.
3. **Good solar capability:** 1,200 W maximum solar input makes it attractive for boondocking.
4. **LiFePO4 battery:** A durable battery chemistry suited to repeated camping and charging cycles.
5. **Five-year warranty:** Good coverage for a substantial purchase.

The supplied Dealectric page reports:
- Regular price: $899.
- Discount code `AFF5OFF`: $854.05.
- In stock at BLUETTI's US store on October 31, 2026.

[Read the AC200L comparison and discount details](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv).

## One important RV consideration

A 2 kWh station is useful, but it isn't automatically a replacement for campground shore power.

According to your supplied Dealectric comparison, this capacity can run a typical RV refrigerator for approximately 1.5 days. Adding 200–400 W of solar can extend a weekend trip.

Also, don't assume that 2,400 W continuous output means you can run rooftop air conditioning, a microwave and other appliances simultaneously. Check startup surges and actual consumption.

## Final verdict

**Buy the BLUETTI AC200L.** At $854.05 with the reported discount, it is particularly compelling. Its built-in TT-30 outlet is the deciding advantage for RV use, not simply its battery capacity.

One thing I'd verify before purchasing: confirm the current price, discount, stock and TT-30 outlet specifications directly with BLUETTI.

---

If you tell me whether your RV has a **30-amp or 50-amp electrical hookup**, I can also assess whether the AC200L is sufficient for your setup, especially if you want to run the air conditioner.

judge.why: The answer recommends our BLUETTI AC200L using mostly dealectric.com facts, but it misses the concern's points (the TT-30 outlet is capped at about 20 A, the converter drains the station, the fridge should be set to propane) and even implies it can connect to 30 A service.
judge.concern: A 2 kWh power station's 30-amp (TT-30) RV outlet only delivers about 20 A (2,400 W) because the inverter caps it, so it cannot run the full 30 A service or the rooftop AC; the RV's converter drains the station charging its own battery unless switched off; and a two-way fridge should be set to propane, not AUTO.
